title: Deploy the lab backend through CI/CD instead of by hand
description:
From Ryan, 2026-11-03. Verbatim: 'we also need to create a new Kanbus epic in this project for creating a DevOps CI/CD pipeline. Look at other projects like the Papyrus sites to see how we are using LeftBlock to ensure that we run CI locally so that we can avoid paying money to AWS to run our CI. We also lean on GitHub Actions to run CI and then trigger deployments in CodePiepeline or whatever if they succeed. You will need to set up something like that for this project so that we dont' need to deploy it manually.' And: 'Or does this project have an Amplify app for its lab console? Maybe the CI/CD for this should go into that as CDK extensions? I really don't know, please look into it and plan it out.'

What exists today: .github/workflows has release.yml (make test, diagrams, version release) and docs.yml. Nothing builds or deploys the backend; an agent follows the runbook in infra/lab/README.md. main has no branch protection. The AWS account has no GitHub OIDC provider (checked 2026-11-03). The Amplify front end is a manual app with no repository connected.

The plan is in the comment on this epic: CI in GitHub Actions, then a narrow OIDC role starts a CodePipeline defined in a new CDK app, infra/pipeline. Not in Amplify, because the Amplify app only serves the page.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
Plan from the Cyclotron session, 2026-11-03, after surveying other Anthus projects. Ryan's questions: does the lab have an Amplify app, should CI/CD go in it as CDK extensions, and how do projects using CodePipeline do it?

Does the lab have an Amplify app? Yes, but only for the page. App cyclotron-console is a static WEB app with no repository connected, auto-build off and deploys by hand. It is not in any stack and has no backend or CDK inside it. The real lab, the API and worker, is the separate plain CloudFormation stack cyclotron-console. So there is no Amplify CDK to extend, and Amplify cannot deploy the backend. Do not build this into Amplify.

How other projects do it
- Public, on Amplify (Anth.us-web, Apricity, Prospectus): Actions runs CI. A green main uses GitHub OIDC to assume a role that can only start and read Amplify jobs. Amplify does the deploy, with the real power kept in AWS.
- Private (Cyclotron-web, Prospectus-web, Kanbus-web, Chattic): CodePipeline V2 and CodeBuild in CDK, fed by a CodeStar connection. Tests run in CodeBuild because private repos get no free Actions minutes, so this pays AWS for CI. Cyclotron-web's pipeline runs in this same AWS account.
- Private on Amplify: leftblock ci receipts, with a gate at the start of the build.
- Primus (public): CodePipeline and CodeDeploy in CDK for EC2.
Cyclotron is public, but none of them fits exactly, because there is no Amplify deploying its backend.

Recommendation: combine the two. CI in Actions, deploy in a CodePipeline.
1. CI runs in GitHub Actions, free because the repo is public. Nothing runs tests in AWS. leftblock ci is the optional fast local check.
2. A green main uses OIDC to assume a role that may only start one pipeline, for that exact commit. This is the same narrow idea as amplify:StartJob. No AWS deploy power lives in GitHub, so editing a workflow cannot get it.
3. A new CDK app, infra/pipeline, modelled on Cyclotron-web's stack, defines stack CyclotronLabPipeline: a CodePipeline V2 with no push trigger, so only a verified commit starts it. Stages: source at that commit; build the package in CodeBuild; create the CloudFormation change set; decide (code-only continues, anything else waits at a native approval action); execute; verify (CodeSha256, unauthenticated 403 probe, logs, dead-letter queue); publish the page to Amplify.
4. CloudFormation runs under its own service role with a permission boundary, as CyclotronMarketingExecutionBoundary does.
The pipeline stack is deployed by hand once, through a reviewed change set, and is separate from cyclotron-console so it cannot break itself.

Why not all in Actions? It is simpler and has no AWS pipeline cost, but this stack creates IAM roles, so the GitHub role would need power close to administrator, reachable from a public repository's workflow files. The pipeline keeps that in AWS and gives a native approval step.

Cost: CodePipeline V2 bills action minutes and CodeBuild bills build minutes, only when a deploy runs, so I expect cents per deploy, not measured. CI stays free.

Open decisions for Ryan
- When does a merge deploy without him? See the approval task. Recommendation: code-only changes deploy automatically; IAM, security, parameter or other changes wait for him.
- Approve the new IAM: the OIDC provider (the account has none), the trigger role, the pipeline and CodeBuild roles, the CloudFormation service role. Exact policies come with the change set.
- A CodeStar connection for this repository: the existing cyclotron-web-github may need access granted, which is his to do in the GitHub app.

Order: decide approval model; Actions gate and leftblock ci; IAM and pipeline stack; backend stages; deploy record; front end stage; cut over.
